causes.name: Statelessness
causes.summary: Thailand has one of the world’s largest registered stateless populations; the opportunity is integration, legal identity, education-to-work continuity, and family support.
metrics: ~600,000 registered stateless people (UNHCR)
169,241 stateless children (UNICEF, Jun 2024)
335,000 long-term residents + 142,000 children covered by accelerated pathway
42,000 working-age refugees eligible for work permits in Oct 2025 pilot
G Code allows school access, but vocational/university often require national ID
notes: Pilot must be legally careful, screened case-by-case, and should not promise citizenship.
Mirror Foundation warned statelessness has ~600–700 cases across ~7 categories; define segment before program design.

causes.name: Dog Rescue
causes.summary: Dog rescue is the emotional donor engine and the operational SE opportunity; CNVR works but owned-dog abandonment keeps replenishing the street population.
metrics: 1.3M owned dogs in Greater Bangkok; 66% roam freely
Nakhon Pathom dog ownership: 30.5%, highest in Greater Bangkok
400,000+ CNVR operations → 24.7% street-dog density reduction
64% of residents in 3-round CNVR areas report fewer dogs vs. 25% control
Owned dog sterilization: 53% vs. vaccination: 84% = 31-point gap
notes: Dr. Ala shared 3 peer-reviewed CNVR papers.
Soi Dog insight: rescue stories move donors more than CNVR stories.
Verify current Soi Dog totals directly; 1.177M April 2024 is confirmed, later 1.6M+/21 teams needs direct confirmation.

causes.name: Homelessness & Poverty / Joblessness
causes.summary: Official homeless numbers understate reality; Center of Dreams/BCH offers a concrete benchmark for meals, rehab beds, 90-day stays, and funding fragility.
metrics: Official homeless count: 4,500 national (2022)
Bangkok one-night count: 1,274
Real estimate: 20,000–40,000+ (NGO/academic estimate)
Center of Dreams: ~700 meals/day, ~20 rehab beds, 90-day stays
Myanmar migrant workers: 2–3M registered, 1–2M unregistered
notes: Need resident outcomes data and successor funding status from BCH.
Elderly homeless is an under-visible segment.

causes.name: Child Education
causes.summary: Stateless and migrant children can enter school but often hit a documentation cliff at vocational/university level; mental-health support is also thin.
metrics: 169,241 registered stateless children
Primary enrollment protected through G Code since 2018
Upper secondary / vocational / university blocked by documentation friction
Childline: ~70,000 contacts/year, ~900 cases, ~10% full resolution — needs direct verification
Children’s mental health waitlists: attribute as Childline observation unless verified
notes: Need Childline stats from Saidek and a safe attribution approach.
Education support is politically/socially sensitive, especially for migrant/stateless children.

strategy.title: Core argument
strategy.body: Thailand’s fertility rate fell from 6.1 in 1960 to 1.0 in 2024. The working-age population may shrink by 8–10M by 2050. Stateless people already in Thailand are a demographic lifeline if legal identity, education, and work pathways are unlocked.

strategy.title: Compound model
strategy.body: No known Thailand organization combines stateless family integration with dog rescue in one physical compound. The model turns two problems into one system: families receive identity/housing/work/community; dogs receive rehabilitation/adoption; SE dog services help fund human services.

strategy.title: Differentiators
strategy.body: Property acquired; 4+ engaged NGO threads; policy window around work permits; Nakhon Pathom dog-ownership data supports location; dog rescue gives emotionally legible donor narrative.

strategy.title: Mirror lessons
strategy.body: Start narrow, build from cases/data, use legally safe pilots, separate care from citizenship promises, make projects economically sustainable, and design data capture from day one.

options: Social Enterprise Promotion Act route or complement — 70% profit reinvestment requirement
warnings: Tax-deductibility must be designed up front with a specialist.
Do not build a donor deck that implies legal outcomes TF cannot guarantee.

benchmarks: Childline Thailand: ~30M THB/year — needs direct verification
Center of Dreams/BCH: ~16.5M THB Citi Foundation grant
Soi Dog: donation-based; official annual budget still needed
revenueStreams: Dog services SE revenue: grooming, training, boarding, vet clinic, cafe/retail, adoption fees

Get Childline stateless child call volumes, resolution rates, quote
Get K. Saks work-permit pilot numbers and family stories
Get BCH resident outcomes, quote, and successor funding answer
Confirm Mirror tax-deductibility status, office count, and statelessness case stats
presentation: Define exact target population segment for pilot
Build donor narrative: emotionally clear, legally precise
Finalize registration path and SE relationship
